scope: Independent source-only audit of inactive pending-queue microbenchmark rebound to v16

Nine core runner function ASTs, including workload cases, identity/sample acceptance and cleanup logic, match the reviewed v3. All 19 case schedules retain ten measured pairs balanced five per ordering, the same seeds and one warmup pair.

The exact v16 specification preserves 23 baseline cases, 166 library and 17 integration controls and 10 full targets. Same-job witness and illustrative workflow require a successful v16 qualification before measuring; six helper pins are checked. The witness relies on trusted workflow ordering rather than being an independent signature.
All six static Python controls pass independently with exact reviewed source inputs and checkout helper paths.
decision: No blocker found within source and static-test scope. Keep the prototype inactive until the full v16 correctness qualification has passed in the same job.
limits: No Cargo, Rust compilation, Clippy, native test, actual benchmark, hosted run or performance ranking was performed.
The witness and illustrative workflow were not exercised end-to-end; helper checks cover pinned files, not dependency bytes or live execution.
Synthetic completion does not establish Kafka delivery, durability, production readiness or aggregate memory bounds.
A shared x86 runner and focused queue microbenchmark cannot establish a fastest-worldwide claim.
